stories.title: One Person Injured in Shooting Near Russell Field in North Cambridge
stories.dek: Police said one person was hospitalized after a shooting near an athletic field off Rindge Avenue on Tuesday afternoon.
body: One person was injured in a shooting near Russell Field in North Cambridge on Tuesday afternoon, according to Cambridge police, as reported by Boston.com.

Police said they received multiple calls reporting gunshots at about 3:20 p.m. The field sits off Rindge Avenue near the Alewife MBTA station and is used by sports teams from Cambridge Rindge and Latin School, Boston.com reported.

Emergency responders found one person with injuries related to the shooting and took the victim to a local hospital, according to a Cambridge Police Department press release cited by Boston.com. Police said the victim's condition was not known. The victim was not identified.

A section of Rindge Avenue was closed off with police tape while investigators worked at the scene, according to the report. Police said they did not believe there was any ongoing danger to the community.

Police did not say whether anyone had been arrested or whether a suspect had been identified. The investigation is ongoing, and police asked anyone with information to call Cambridge police detectives at 617-349-3300.

sources.title: 1 injured in shooting near Cambridge athletic field

stories.title: Acton Teen Pleads Not Guilty to Murder in Deaths of Mother and Brother
stories.dek: A 17-year-old from Acton pleaded not guilty Tuesday in Middlesex Superior Court to murder charges in the August deaths of his mother and younger brother.
body: A 17-year-old from Acton pleaded not guilty Tuesday in Middlesex County Superior Court to charges that he killed his mother and his 14-year-old brother, Boston.com reported.

The teen is charged with murder and assault in the deaths of his mother, 45, and his brother, along with one count of motor vehicle theft, according to the report. Judge Michael A. Sullivan ordered him held without bail under an agreement between prosecutors and the defense, Boston.com reported. His next court date is a scheduling conference on Oct. 27.

Prosecutors allege the deaths occurred on Aug. 11 at the family's home in Acton. According to the Middlesex District Attorney's office, the father asked police to conduct a wellness check after a tutor arrived at the house that evening and got no answer. Officers found both victims inside the home, prosecutors said.

Prosecutors allege the teen left in his mother's car after the killings. Police located him and the vehicle in a Wayland parking lot at about 3:30 a.m. the next day and took him into custody without incident, according to the report.

He was first arraigned in Concord District Court on Aug. 13, and a grand jury indicted him on Oct. 1, Boston.com reported. His attorney did not respond to requests for comment. The charges are allegations, and he is presumed innocent unless proven guilty in court.

sources.title: Acton teen who allegedly used AI for violent 'fantasies' pleads not guilty to killing family members

stories.title: Hadley Man Pleads Guilty to Importing and Selling Russian Plutonium
stories.dek: A 44-year-old Hadley man pleaded guilty in federal court to five counts, including importing nuclear material from Russia and mailing hazardous materials to customers.
body: A Hadley man pleaded guilty in federal court to illegally importing plutonium from Russia and selling it to customers in the United States and abroad, according to Boston.com, which cited the U.S. Attorney's Office in Massachusetts.

Jacob Miller, 44, pleaded guilty to five counts: being a felon in possession of ammunition, being a felon in possession of explosive materials, importing nuclear material without lawful authority, mailing hazardous materials, and possession of child pornography, the report said. He had previously been sentenced in 2004 to six months in prison and 10 years of probation for possessing child pornography and an explosive device.

According to prosecutors, Miller ran a business from his home selling samples of chemical elements, directly and through an online retailer. Prosecutors said he mailed plutonium to about 67 customers between December 2020 and March 2025, and sold thallium, another hazardous substance that cannot legally be mailed, to about 71 customers between 2017 and April 2025.

Authorities searched his home in April 2025 and reported finding explosive powder, ammunition and six rifles, which he was barred from having because of his prior convictions, Boston.com reported. Prosecutors said his laptop and phone contained child sexual abuse material. He was arrested on April 9, 2025.

The nuclear import charge carries up to 20 years in prison, and the child pornography charge carries a mandatory minimum of 10 years because of his prior conviction, according to the report. U.S. District Judge Mark G. Mastroianni scheduled sentencing for Jan. 21, 2027.

sources.title: Mass. man pleads guilty to selling Russian plutonium

stories.title: Brockton Man, 18, Struck and Killed Crossing Route 44 in Raynham
stories.dek: An 18-year-old Brockton man died after being hit by an SUV while crossing New State Highway in Raynham early Tuesday, officials said.
body: An 18-year-old man from Brockton was struck and killed while crossing New State Highway in Raynham early Tuesday morning, according to Raynham police and fire officials, as reported by Boston.com.

The crash happened at about 6:15 a.m. near 430 New State Highway, a section of Route 44 lined with several businesses, including a gas station and a Dunkin', the report said. Officials said a Honda CR-V traveling west on the highway struck the man.

First responders treated him at the scene and took him to Boston Medical Center-South in Brockton, where he was later pronounced dead, according to officials. Authorities had not publicly identified him.

The driver of the Honda, a 37-year-old Taunton man, remained at the scene, officials said. He and a passenger were taken by ambulance to Morton Hospital in Taunton to be evaluated, according to Boston.com.
Officials described the investigation as preliminary. The report did not say whether any charges were being considered.

stories.title: Inquest Finds Fatal Cambridge Police Shooting Justified; Bodycam Footage Released
stories.dek: A judge ruled that officers acted reasonably when they shot a 64-year-old Watertown man in Central Square in August, and the district attorney will not file charges.
body: A judicial inquest has found that Cambridge police officers were justified when they fatally shot a 64-year-old Watertown man in Central Square in August, Boston.com reported. The Cambridge Police Department released body-worn camera footage of the encounter.

The shooting happened on Temple Street shortly before 8 p.m. on Aug. 21, according to the report. A security guard at 675 Massachusetts Ave. had called 911 about people loitering in a nearby private parking lot, and Officer Donald Conrad approached a parked car where the man was in the driver's seat.

According to the inquest findings described by Boston.com, the man reached under the seat and pulled out a gun as Conrad ordered him out of the car, ignored three commands to drop it, and pointed it at Officer David Kerns, who struggled with him. Conrad fired several shots and Officer James Nestor fired once, the judge found. The man died at the scene. The judge found that less than a minute passed between the start of the encounter and the shooting, and that the gun was loaded.

In a nine-page report, Judge Holly Broadbent concluded that the officers' use of force was objectively reasonable and that any reasonable officer would have believed officers and civilians faced imminent danger, according to the report.

Middlesex District Attorney Marian Ryan's office accepted the findings and will not pursue criminal charges, Boston.com reported. Cambridge police said the footage provides context for a rapidly evolving situation, said no officers were seriously hurt, and offered condolences to the man's family.

sources.title: Fatal shooting by Cambridge police deemed justified, bodycam footage released

stories.title: Traffic Stop on Washington Street in Dorchester Leads to Gun Arrest
stories.dek: Boston police said they found a loaded handgun hidden in a car's radio casing after stopping a Quincy man driving on a suspended license.
body: Boston police arrested a Quincy man Sunday night after a traffic stop on Washington Street in Dorchester, where officers said they found a loaded handgun concealed inside the car's radio casing, according to a department release.

Police said officers from District C-11 were near 156 Washington Street at about 9:17 p.m. on Oct. 4 when they saw a man walk from a vehicle into a store. A records check showed the vehicle operator's license was suspended, according to the release.

Officers said the man went back and forth between the store and the vehicle several times without starting the car. After briefly losing sight of him, officers saw the vehicle drive away and stopped it near 54 Washington Street, police said.

As the driver got out, officers noticed that the gear shift box and radio appeared to have been tampered with and saw the handle of a firearm inside the radio casing, according to police. They recovered a Glock 19 9mm handgun loaded with 11 rounds, the release said.

Police identified the driver as Johnny Williams Delacruz, 27, of Quincy. He was expected to be arraigned in Dorchester District Court on charges including carrying a loaded firearm without a license, possession of ammunition without an FID card, receiving stolen property and driving with a suspended license, police said. He was also cited for motor vehicle violations. The charges are allegations, and he is presumed innocent.

sources.title: Traffic Stop Leads to Suspect Arrested and Firearm Recovered in Dorchester

stories.title: Bloom, a Matcha Cafe by Day and Cocktail Bar by Night, Opens in the Seaport
stories.dek: The 20-seat bar at 60 Seaport Blvd. serves tea in the daytime and cocktails in the evening, according to Boston.com.
body: Bloom, a 20-seat tea cafe that turns into a craft cocktail bar at night, was set to open Oct. 6 in the Seaport, Boston.com reported. The bar is in the atrium at 60 Seaport Blvd., in the space formerly occupied by Zazibar.

According to the report, Bloom serves matcha and hojicha from 11 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. and cocktails from 5 p.m. to 11 p.m. It will be closed Mondays for its first two weeks before moving to a seven-day schedule, with limited hours and a smaller menu at first.

The project is led by Christian Doan, an investor in the nearby izakaya Mai, along with Mai partner Ray Lee, who has run tea shops in Boston for about two decades, and co-founder Isabelle Lin, Boston.com reported. Chef Chompon Boonnak of Mahaniyom and Merai, Markus Yao, formerly of Shojo, and bartender Iruma Shibuya are also involved, according to the report.

The daytime menu includes matcha flights, genmaicha and aged teas, most sourced from MEM Tea in Cambridge, the report said. The evening menu includes classic cocktails, a martini service with Japanese and Vietnamese gins, a matcha twist on the espresso martini, and a shochu highball infused with shiso and kombu. A food menu with milk bread sandwiches, curry rice bowls and bar snacks is coming, according to Boston.com.

The space was designed by Bangkok firm Minick\Bom with wood, greenery and lantern-style lighting inspired by Japanese botanical gardens, the report said. The owners told Boston.com they wanted a nature-focused room as a counterpoint to the Seaport's corporate feel.

sources.title: Bloom, a daytime cafe and evening craft cocktail bar, opens in the Seaport

stories.title: The Moseley Opens on Ninth Floor of South Station Tower
stories.dek: A 10,000-square-foot restaurant from Chicago-based Episcope Hospitality opened Oct. 5 above South Station with views of the city skyline, Boston.com reported.
body: A new restaurant called The Moseley opened to the public on Oct. 5 on the ninth floor of South Station Tower at 680 Atlantic Ave., Boston.com reported. The roughly 10,000-square-foot space looks out over the downtown skyline.

The restaurant is run by Chicago-based Episcope Hospitality, whose CEO and co-founder, David Morton, is the son of Morton's The Steakhouse co-founder Arnold Morton, according to the report. Morton described the style to Boston.com as casual fine dining built around quality ingredients and simple preparation. Episcope also runs two other concepts in the tower that are open only to tenants and residents.

The Moseley serves lunch and dinner Monday through Friday from 11:30 a.m. to 9 p.m. and dinner on Saturday from 5 p.m. to 9 p.m., and it hosts private events, the report said. The menu includes a crab cake, tuna tartare, a lobster roll, a dry-aged sirloin burger, a 10-ounce filet mignon and miso black cod, according to Boston.com. The report did not list prices.

Boston firm Perkins&Will designed the room with curved white oak ceilings, wood paneling and bronze accents intended to recall late-1800s rail cars, according to the report. The restaurant is named for Alex Moseley, who ran a leather business on nearby South Street in that era and helped shape the Leather District.
South Station Tower is a 51-story mixed-use building that was completed in 2025, Boston.com reported.

sources.title: A new restaurant with sweeping skyline views opens above South Station

stories.title: Person Stabbed in Downtown Crossing Suffers Life-Threatening Injuries
stories.dek: Boston police said a person was stabbed Friday night near Tremont Street and Temple Place, and homicide detectives were called to investigate.
body: A person was stabbed Friday night near Tremont Street and Temple Place in Downtown Crossing and was taken to a hospital with life-threatening injuries, Boston police said, according to Boston.com.

Officers were called at about 10:55 p.m. for a report of an assault in progress, police spokesperson Officer James Moccia told Boston.com. When officers arrived, they found a person who had been stabbed, police said.
Emergency medical crews treated the victim at the scene before taking the person to a local hospital, according to the report. Police did not publicly identify the victim or release the victim's age.
Homicide detectives were also called to investigate, Boston.com reported. Police did not describe what led up to the stabbing or provide any information about a possible suspect.
As of Sunday morning, no arrests had been made, according to police. The investigation is ongoing, and police did not release any further details about the case.

sources.title: Person stabbed in Downtown Crossing, hospitalized with life-threatening injuries

stories.title: Smashing Pumpkins Mark 'Mellon Collie' Anniversary With Three-Hour TD Garden Show
stories.dek: The band played two sets built around its 1995 double album at TD Garden on Oct. 2, according to a Boston.com review.
body: The Smashing Pumpkins played a nearly three-hour concert at TD Garden on Friday, Oct. 2, built around their 1995 double album "Mellon Collie and the Infinite Sadness," according to a review by Terence Cawley for Boston.com.

The stop on the band's "Rats in a Cage" tour was billed as two distinct sets marking the album's 30th anniversary, with a 20-minute intermission, the review said. The band performed 16 of the album's 28 tracks rather than the full record, according to Boston.com.

The lineup included Billy Corgan, James Iha, Jimmy Chamberlin, new guitarist Kiki Wong and bassist Jack Bates, the review said. The first set opened with "1979" and "Bullet With Butterfly Wings" and included "Tonight, Tonight" and "Porcelina of the Vast Oceans" before closing with the album's title track. The second set of 14 songs featured "Disarm," "Mayonaise" and "Cherub Rock" and ended with "Superchrist," which included several drum solos from Chamberlin.

Cawley praised the first set and singled out Chamberlin's drumming and the guitar work of Corgan, Iha and Wong, according to the review. He found the second set uneven, writing that songs from the band's more recent albums drew a muted response and that the closing number worked more as a drum showcase than a finale.
Overall, the reviewer concluded that the show's ambition was worthwhile despite a less focused second half, Boston.com reported.

sources.title: Review & setlist: Smashing Pumpkins honor 'Mellon Collie' with 3-hour extravaganza

stories.title: Gorillaz Bring 'The Mountain' Tour to a Sold-Out TD Garden
stories.dek: Damon Albarn's band played a two-hour show with guest performers and a tour debut of the rarely played '5/4' on Oct. 1, according to a Boston.com review.
body: Gorillaz played a sold-out show at TD Garden on Thursday, Oct. 1, on the band's tour supporting its ninth studio album, "The Mountain," according to a review by Emily Turner for Boston.com. Deltron 3030 and Little Simz opened.

The roughly two-hour set featured frontman Damon Albarn with bassist Seye Adelekan, guitarist Jeff Wootton and a live ensemble of more than a dozen musicians, the review said. Guest performers included Little Simz, Del the Funky Homosapien, Posdnuos of De La Soul, Bootie Brown and Kara Jackson, according to the posted setlist.

The band performed "5/4," a song from its 2001 debut album, for the first time on the tour, Boston.com reported. The 22-song set mixed songs from the new album with older material including "19-2000," "El Mañana" and "Kids With Guns," and the encore closed with "Feel Good Inc." and "Clint Eastwood."

Jamie Hewlett's animated visuals, featuring the band's cartoon characters, played across the screens throughout the night, and a puppet named Alan appeared on stage, according to the review. Before the show, Albarn walked through the crowd, signed albums and posed for photos with fans, Boston.com reported.

Turner wrote that the set balanced new and older songs without feeling like a nostalgia act, singled out Little Simz as one of the night's strongest performers, and said the visuals were central to the show rather than decoration, according to the review.

sources.title: Review & setlist: Gorillaz brings '5/4' tour debut and visual spectacle to TD Garden

stories.title: Smashburgers, Uyghur Noodles and a Spice Festival Lead Boston Dining News
stories.dek: Boston.com's Oct. 2 roundup covers new locations for 7th Street Burger, a Watertown Uyghur takeout spot, a downtown cafe and a West Roxbury burger restaurant.
body: Several restaurants are opening or expanding around Greater Boston this fall, according to a dining roundup published Oct. 2 by Boston.com.

New York-based smashburger chain 7th Street Burger, which already has locations on Newbury Street and in South Boston, plans to open a 46-seat restaurant at 880 Broadway in Saugus in October and a 22-seat location at 37 Brattle St. in Harvard Square in early 2027, the report said.

In Watertown, Adila Sadir, who runs Silk Road Uyghur Cuisine in Cambridge, is preparing to open Badam Uyghur Cuisine at 58 Mt. Auburn St. in November, according to Boston.com. The roughly 16-seat spot will focus on takeout, with hand-pulled noodles, lamb kebabs and rice pilaf.

Downtown, MOTW Coffee & Pastries was scheduled to open in mid-October at 45 Broad St., Boston.com reported. The cafe is the retail arm of Muslims of the World, a nonprofit that provides humanitarian aid, and plans to serve chai, lattes, matcha and tiramisu.

In West Roxbury, Yeanie's Burgers and Social opened in September at 1761 Centre St. after delays, according to the report. It is the seventh restaurant for Phi Pham and his wife, Yeanie Bach, and shares a menu of smash burgers, fried chicken sandwiches and shakes with its Dorchester location.
The roundup also listed Spicetober Fest, a free festival of spicy food, chef demonstrations and live music held Saturday, Oct. 3, at City Hall Plaza.

sources.title: 5 best new restaurant openings and dining updates in Boston (October 2, 2026)

stories.title: Boston Magazine's October Guide Highlights New Restaurants and Bars
stories.dek: The magazine's monthly list includes a Montreal-inspired spot in Fort Point, a soju distillery in Mission Hill and a rum lounge coming to South Boston.
body: Boston Magazine's October guide to new places to eat and drink around Greater Boston lists more than 20 new or changing restaurants, cafes and bars, according to the list by food editor Rachel Leah Blumenthal.

Among new restaurants, the magazine highlighted Celine at 324 A St. in Fort Point, a Montreal-inspired French-Canadian spot from the team behind SRV, Gufo and Salty Pig, and Zhu at 903 Boylston St. in Back Bay, a multi-level Chinese seafood and dim sum restaurant in soft opening. In Groton, chef Will Gilson of Cambridge's Puritan & Company is behind Puritan Tavern, a more casual New England tavern at 20 Station Ave., the guide said.

Drink-focused openings include Namu Distilling Co. at 89 Heath St. in Mission Hill, which the magazine described as New England's first soju distillery, and Overproof Cocktail Lounge, a rum-focused bar at 85 Damrell St. in South Boston expected to open later in October, according to the guide. The list also includes Bloom in the Seaport, C'Yool, a Yemeni cafe and bakery in the South End, and Pomona Cafe & Wine Bar in East Boston.

The guide also noted established names trying something new. Brookline Lunch has expanded to 108 L St. in South Boston, Quincy's Rubato, led by Top Chef finalist Laurence Louie, was set to begin regular dinner service Oct. 9, and the Lao pop-up Phaeng & Phiu has taken up residence at Shore Leave in the South End for its final months, according to Boston Magazine.
The magazine reported that Shore Leave and its sibling bars are scheduled to close at the end of the year.

stories.title: Dorchester Man, 20, Charged With Murder in Whitfield Street Shooting
stories.dek: A 20-year-old Dorchester man pleaded not guilty and was held without bail in the fatal shooting of a man near 7 Whitfield St., the Boston Globe reported.
body: A 20-year-old Dorchester man has been charged with murder in a fatal shooting on Whitfield Street in Dorchester, the Boston Globe reported.

Joseph Bailey was arraigned Thursday, Oct. 1, in the Dorchester Division of Boston Municipal Court, where he was ordered held without bail, according to the Globe. Online court records show he pleaded not guilty, the newspaper reported. No attorney was listed for him in the records.

Police said the shooting happened shortly before 5:40 p.m. on Wednesday, Sept. 30, near 7 Whitfield St., according to the Globe. A man was killed. Authorities had not released his name or age, the newspaper reported.
Police said Bailey was arrested following an investigation, and a spokesperson for the Suffolk District Attorney's Office confirmed the murder charge, the Globe reported.
Bailey is scheduled to return to court on Oct. 22. The charge is an allegation, and he is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

sources.title: Man, 20, charged with murder in fatal Dorchester shooting

stories.title: Woman Killed When Vehicle Strikes Building on Faulkner Hospital Campus
stories.dek: A woman sitting on a bench was killed and two people in the vehicle were hurt when it crashed into a building at the Jamaica Plain hospital, the Boston Globe reported.
body: A woman was killed Thursday morning when a vehicle crashed into a building on the Brigham and Women's Faulkner Hospital campus in Jamaica Plain, the Boston Globe reported. She had been sitting on a bench outside the building, according to the report.

The vehicle struck the Belkin House, a standalone building the hospital leases to a dialysis clinic, and came to rest between the parking garage entrance and the building's front steps, the Globe reported. A witness told the newspaper the crash happened at about 11 a.m. The woman was taken to the hospital's emergency department, where she died. Her name and age were not released.

Two people in the vehicle were injured and treated at the hospital, according to the Globe. The crash ruptured a gas line, and more than 30 people were evacuated. Boston EMS paramedics who saw the crash called 911 and requested firefighters, and four paramedics were evaluated for exposure, the report said.

Boston Police Superintendent Paul McLaughlin said the preliminary investigation indicated the crash was not deliberate and that police were not treating it as a crime, the Globe reported. A Mass General Brigham spokesperson offered condolences to the woman's family and to those injured and said staff could use an employee assistance program.

The Belkin House was closed as a precaution while crews checked gas lines, and dialysis patients were directed to other locations, according to the report. The cause of the crash remains under investigation.

sources.title: 'A very tragic situation': Woman sitting on bench outside Faulkner Hospital killed after vehicle slammed into building

stories.title: Man Arrested in Alleged Sexual Assaults in Cambridge Gym Locker Room
stories.dek: Cambridge police said a 40-year-old man entered the women's locker room at a Porter Square gym Thursday morning and assaulted people inside.
body: Cambridge police arrested a man Thursday morning who they say entered the women's locker room at a gym in Porter Square and sexually assaulted people inside, the Boston Globe reported.

According to police, the initial report came in shortly after 9 a.m., and the suspect was arrested at 9:22 a.m. Police did not name the gym, but Planet Fitness confirmed to the Globe that the incident happened at its location. Police did not say how many people were assaulted. One woman was taken to a hospital for evaluation, the newspaper reported.
Police identified the man as Laquan Holland, 40, according to the Globe. Details of his arraignment were not immediately available.

Court records show Holland was charged in August in Cambridge District Court with failing to register as a sex offender, a charge that was dropped the same day, the Globe reported. In 2006, he pleaded guilty to child rape and indecent assault charges, according to the newspaper.

Planet Fitness said it is committed to providing a safe environment, has canceled the man's membership and is cooperating with law enforcement, according to the Globe. The investigation is ongoing. The new allegations have not been proven in court, and Holland is presumed innocent.

sources.title: Man allegedly commits sexual assaults in women's locker room at Cambridge gym, police say

stories.title: Mayor Wu Endorses Gov. Healey and Lt. Gov. Driscoll for Re-Election
stories.dek: Boston Mayor Michelle Wu formally backed the Healey-Driscoll ticket on Thursday, pointing to their work together on transit, housing and public safety.
body: Boston Mayor Michelle Wu formally endorsed Gov. Maura Healey and Lt. Gov. Kim Driscoll for re-election on Thursday morning, according to WBUR, which published a State House News Service report by Colin A. Young.

In announcing the endorsement, Wu cited a partnership to build a city and state that work for everyone, the report said. She thanked the Healey administration for its work on lowering costs, housing, public safety and opportunity, and said she looks forward to continuing to work with the administration. Wu also discussed the endorsement on WBUR's Morning Edition, highlighting the two leaders' work together on the MBTA and commuter rail.

Healey responded by calling Wu a fantastic partner and a champion for Boston residents, according to the report. She pointed to the summer's events in the city, including the World Cup, and said she was grateful to work with the mayor.

Both Democrats are the first women elected to their offices, but WBUR reported they are not known for a close political relationship. The two backed opposing candidates in two Democratic state Senate primaries last month, and Healey declined to say whether she supported Wu on the eve of Wu's 2025 mayoral primary against Josh Kraft, according to the report.

Republican candidate for governor Mike Minogue posted a video on social media Tuesday mocking Healey and Wu, recalling the two being booed at Fenway Park in April, WBUR reported. Healey and Wu were scheduled to appear together Thursday at Otis Elementary School in East Boston to mark school building upgrades.

sources.title: Boston Mayor Wu endorses Gov. Healey for re-election

stories.title: Police Release Photos of Person Sought in Roxbury Stabbing
stories.dek: Boston police are asking the public to help identify a person wanted in connection with a stabbing near Warren Street that left a victim with a facial wound.
body: Boston police have released photos of a person they want to identify in connection with a stabbing in Roxbury on Tuesday evening, Boston.com reported.

Officers were called to the area of 201 Warren St. shortly after 7 p.m. and found the victim in nearby Kensington Park, according to police. The victim had a serious cut to the face and was taken to a local hospital with injuries police described as not life-threatening, the report said. The victim was not identified.

Officers searched the surrounding area but did not locate the person responsible, police said. The department later released images of a person of interest and asked for the public's help, according to Boston.com.
Police did not describe what led to the stabbing, and the report did not say whether the victim and the person being sought knew each other.

Anyone with information is asked to call District B-2 detectives at 617-343-4275. Tips can be shared anonymously by calling 1-800-494-TIPS or through the Boston Police Department website, police said. The investigation is ongoing.

sources.title: Police reveal photos of person of interest in Roxbury face stabbing

stories.title: Missing 14-Year-Old Mattapan Girl Found, Boston Police Say
stories.dek: Boston police announced that a 14-year-old girl reported missing from Mattapan in mid-September had been located.
body: A 14-year-old girl from Mattapan who had been missing since mid-September has been found, Boston police announced Monday night, according to Boston.com. Police released no other details about where or how she was located.
The girl was reported missing on Sept. 17, according to the report. Police said she was last seen at about 9 a.m. on Sept. 16 in the area of Hillsboro Road in Mattapan.

While she was missing, police said she was known to spend time in the Grove Hall area, along Boylston Street and near Copley, and asked anyone who saw her to contact District B-3 detectives, Boston.com reported. The department had also invited the public to share anonymous tips by phone or through its website.
Police first asked the public for help locating the girl in a missing person alert, which Boston.com published on Oct. 1. The news site later updated its report after police said she had been found.

Police had asked anyone with information to call 911 or District B-3 detectives at 617-343-4712 during the search. After announcing that she had been located, the department released no further information about her case, according to the report.

sources.title: Missing 14-year-old Mattapan girl found

stories.title: Five Boston Restaurants to Watch in October
stories.dek: Boston.com's October picks include a Yemeni coffeehouse in the South End, a Roxbury jazz cafe, a Mission Hill soju distillery, a Back Bay sushi pop-up and a three-level Chinese restaurant.
body: Boston.com has named five new or recently opened restaurants it is eager to try in October, in a list by Jillian Dara published Oct. 1.

C'Yool, a new Yemeni coffeehouse and bakery at 600 Harrison Ave. in the South End, roasts its beans on site and serves breads such as sabaya along with traditional coffee drinks, according to the list. In Roxbury, Jazz Urbane Cafe at 2300 Washington St. has opened as a live music and arts venue with a restaurant menu that includes brunch dishes and shrimp and grits, with film screenings and theater planned, Boston.com reported.

NAMU Distilling Company, a Korean-American craft distillery at 89 Heath St. in Mission Hill founded by Will Blessing and Josh Moss, makes soju and gin and serves anju, small dishes meant to accompany drinks, the list said. Menu prices range from $7 for olives to $25 for braised short rib, according to the report.
In Back Bay, Shuden Bar runs as a weekly pop-up on Wednesdays from 4 to 9 p.m. at The Irving inside The Lenox, 61 Exeter St., serving hand-rolled sushi and Japanese whiskies, according to Boston.com.

Also in Back Bay, Zhu has opened in soft-opening mode at 903 Boylston St., the former Lir space, the list said. Chef Joanna Zhu's three-level restaurant features an open dim sum bar, dumplings and handmade noodles with lobster, Boston.com reported.

sources.title: 5 restaurants we can't wait to try in October

stories.title: Ringo Starr and His All-Starr Band Play Sold-Out MGM Music Hall
stories.dek: The 86-year-old former Beatle led a 21-song set of his own songs and his bandmates' hits at MGM Music Hall at Fenway on Sept. 30, according to a Boston.com review.
body: Ringo Starr and His All-Starr Band played a sold-out show at MGM Music Hall at Fenway on Wednesday, Sept. 30, according to a review by Abby Patkin for Boston.com.

The 86-year-old former Beatle was joined by Steve Lukather of Toto, Colin Hay of Men at Work, Hamish Stuart of Average White Band, drummer Gregg Bissonette, saxophonist Warren Ham and Buck Johnson, the review said. The 21-song set opened with Carl Perkins' "Matchbox" and mixed Starr's Beatles and solo material with hits from his bandmates' catalogs, including "Rosanna," "Down Under," "Pick Up the Pieces" and "Africa."

According to the review, "Yellow Submarine" drew one of the strongest crowd responses, and "Photograph" was a highlight. The show closed with "With a Little Help From My Friends," with an outro of "Give Peace a Chance," Boston.com reported.

Patkin praised Lukather's guitar playing and Hay's vocals, and described Starr's drumming as understated but steady, according to the review. She wrote that a few moments fell flat, including a cover of "Boys" and the newer song "Choose Love," which she found an awkward fit for an otherwise upbeat set.
Overall, the reviewer described the night as a nostalgic, jam-style evening and wrote that Starr remains a strong showman, Boston.com reported.

stories.title: Five-Alarm Fire in Somerville's Teele Square Displaces 43 Residents
stories.dek: A fire at a mixed-use building on Broadway left 43 residents from 32 units without homes and sent two firefighters to the hospital with minor injuries, the Boston Globe reported.
body: A five-alarm fire spread through a mixed-use building in Somerville's Teele Square on Wednesday, displacing 43 residents from 32 apartments, the Boston Globe reported.

The fire broke out at 1135 Broadway, at the corner of Curtis Street, a brick building with apartments upstairs and businesses on the ground floor, including a laundromat and two restaurants, according to the Globe. Medford firefighters returning from another call spotted smoke between the third floor and the roof and reported it, the newspaper said.

The fire peaked shortly before 5 p.m., was brought under control by about 6 p.m. and was largely out by 7 p.m., according to the report. Crews from Revere, Lexington, Everett, Arlington, Chelsea, Medford and Cambridge assisted. All residents got out safely, and two firefighters were treated at a hospital for minor injuries, the Globe reported.

Fire officials said Thursday the fire was confined to third-floor units but spread along the ceilings and beneath the roof across 1137 to 1147 Broadway, according to the newspaper. The third floor and roof sustained heavy fire, smoke and water damage, and the lower floors had extensive water damage. Somerville Fire Chief Charles Breen said many of the ground-floor businesses will likely be closed.

The American Red Cross is helping displaced residents find temporary housing and is working with the city's Board of Health to identify those affected, the Globe reported. The cause of the fire is under investigation.

stories.title: Man Shot in Dorchester Apartment; Homicide Detectives Respond
stories.dek: Boston police said a man was taken to a hospital with life-threatening injuries after a shooting at an apartment on Whitfield Street on Wednesday evening.
body: A man was shot inside an apartment on Whitfield Street in Dorchester on Wednesday evening and was taken to a hospital with life-threatening injuries, officials said, according to the Boston Globe.

Boston police said officers responded at about 5:40 p.m. to a report of a person shot at 7 Whitfield St., the Globe reported. When they arrived, first responders found a man suffering from a gunshot wound, according to police.
The man was taken to a hospital, officials said. His condition was not immediately known, and authorities did not release his name or age, the newspaper reported.

Investigators from the Boston Police Department's homicide unit went to the scene, according to the Globe. Police said the shooting remained under investigation. The report did not include any information about a suspect, and no arrests had been announced.
The Globe described its story as breaking news and said it would be updated as more information became available. The report did not say what led to the shooting or describe any possible suspect.

stories.title: New York Times Adds Seven Boston-Area Restaurants to Its Dining Guide
stories.dek: The newspaper's updated Boston guide now lists 27 restaurants, with new additions in South Boston, the South End, Back Bay, Quincy, Dorchester and downtown, Boston.com reported.
body: The New York Times added seven restaurants to its Boston dining guide on Tuesday, bringing the list to 27 restaurants, according to Boston.com.

The new additions are Dalia, a Spanish-inspired restaurant from chef Nicholas Dixon at 629 West Broadway in South Boston; Baleia, a Portuguese-inspired spot at 264 East Berkeley St. in the South End; and Kaia, a Greek restaurant from chef Junyoung Ma at 370 Harrison Ave., also in the South End, Boston.com reported.

Also added were La Padrona, chef Jody Adams' Italian restaurant inside the Raffles Hotel in Back Bay; Lê Madeline, a Vietnamese restaurant at 409 Hancock St. in Quincy led by executive chef and co-owner Peter Nguyen; McGonagle's, an Irish restaurant from chef Aidan McGee at 367 Neponset Ave. in Dorchester; and Somaek, chef Jamie Bissonnette's Korean restaurant at 11 Temple Place downtown, according to the report.

Several of the additions have drawn national attention before, Boston.com reported. Dalia, which opened in April, appeared on the Times' 2026 list of its 50 favorite U.S. restaurants earlier in September, and McGonagle's was on the newspaper's 2025 list. La Padrona recently ranked second on a USA Today list of the best hotel restaurants in the country, according to the report.
Longtime favorites that remain on the guide include Neptune Oyster, Giulia, Sarma, Toro and Yume Ga Arukara, Boston.com reported.

stories.title: Roxbury Man Charged Federally in Alleged Rhode Island Kidnapping
stories.dek: Federal prosecutors say a 31-year-old Roxbury man forced a person from their Rhode Island home into a car and drove into Massachusetts before crashing on I-93.
body: A 31-year-old Roxbury man has been charged in federal court with kidnapping a person from their home in Rhode Island and driving them into Massachusetts, according to Boston.com, which cited a release from the U.S. Attorney's Office in Massachusetts.
Dominic Hampton-Boyd is charged with kidnapping and with being a felon in possession of a firearm and ammunition, the report said.

Prosecutors allege that on Aug. 12, Hampton-Boyd entered the victim's Rhode Island home, struck the victim with a pistol, forced the victim into a car and asked whether they wanted to "die here or in Boston." According to prosecutors, he then drove into Massachusetts while the victim tried several times to get out of the car.

The victim called 911, prosecutors said. When police tried to pull the car over, Hampton-Boyd allegedly sped up, struck several vehicles on Interstate 93 and crashed, then ran but was caught, according to the report. Police said they recovered a privately made, Glock-style pistol loaded with 9mm ammunition from the car. Prosecutors said prior state convictions, including armed robbery, bar him from having guns or ammunition. The victim was not identified.

Hampton-Boyd is being held in state custody and will appear in federal court in Boston at a later date, Boston.com reported. The kidnapping charge carries a possible sentence of up to life in prison. The charges are allegations, and he is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

sources.title: Police: Alleged kidnapper asked RI victim if they wanted to 'die here or in Boston'

stories.title: Milton Man Killed in Shooting Inside Hyde Park Business
stories.dek: Boston police said a 37-year-old Milton man was fatally shot near 54 Walter Street on Saturday afternoon, and the department's homicide unit is investigating.
body: A 37-year-old man from Milton was shot and killed inside a business on Walter Street in Hyde Park on Saturday afternoon, according to the Boston Police Department.

Officers from District E-18 responded to a radio call at about 1:09 p.m. on Sept. 26 for a person shot inside a business near 54 Walter Street, police said in a release. When they arrived, officers found a man with multiple gunshot wounds, according to the department.
Boston EMS pronounced the man dead at the scene, police said.
The Boston Police Homicide Unit is reviewing the facts and circumstances of the shooting, according to the release. Police did not announce any arrests or release information about a suspect.

Police asked anyone with information to contact homicide detectives at 617-343-4470. Tips can be shared anonymously by calling 1-800-494-TIPS or by texting the word TIP to 27463, according to the department. The department also noted that the Boston Neighborhood Trauma Team offers free emotional support around the clock to residents affected by violence at 617-431-0125.
The investigation remains open, police said.

stories.title: Detectives Seek Two Men in Armed Robbery of Blue Hill Avenue Store
stories.dek: Boston police released images and asked for help identifying two men they say robbed a Dorchester store at gunpoint on Thursday morning.
body: Boston police are asking the public to help identify two men in connection with an armed robbery at a store on Blue Hill Avenue in Dorchester on Thursday morning, according to a department community alert.
Officers from District B-2 responded to a radio call at about 11:15 a.m. on Sept. 24 for an armed robbery at 322 Blue Hill Avenue, police said.

According to the victim's account, as described by police, one of the men pointed a firearm at the victim and demanded money while the second man went behind the counter. The two took all of the cash from the store's register and its lottery register, police said. The men then fled along Lawrence Street toward Normandy Street, according to the alert. The release did not report any injuries.
The department released images of the two men it is seeking. District B-2 detectives are actively investigating, and no arrests had been announced, according to the alert.

Anyone with information is asked to call detectives at 617-343-5628, the number listed in the release. Tips can also be shared anonymously through CrimeStoppers by calling 1-800-494-TIPS, by texting the word TIP to 27463, or through the department's online form, police said.

stories.title: Jonas Brothers, Porchfest and 'Wicked' Top Boston's Sept. 25-27 Weekend
stories.dek: The Boston Globe's weekend guide lists concerts, comedy, festivals, theater and museum openings around the region for Sept. 25 through 27.
body: The Jonas Brothers at TD Garden, the Sam Adams Octoberfest and Brookline Porchfest were among the events highlighted in the Boston Globe's guide to the weekend of Sept. 25 to 27.

The Jonas Brothers were scheduled to play TD Garden on Friday, Sept. 25, at 7:30 p.m., with tickets starting at $69, according to the guide. Role Model was set to perform at Leader Bank Pavilion on Sunday, Sept. 27, with Samia opening. Comedian Craig Robinson had four shows at Laugh Boston on Friday and Saturday, the Globe reported.

The Samuel Adams Boston Brewery at 30 Germania St. was hosting its Octoberfest all weekend, with tickets from $10, while Brookline Porchfest offered free performances across the town on Saturday from 11 a.m. to 6:30 p.m., with a rain date of Oct. 3, the guide said. A free a cappella festival with more than 15 groups was planned for the Riverstage at Herter Park in Allston on Saturday.

On stage, the musical "Wicked" opened the Broadway in Boston season at the Citizens Opera House and runs through Nov. 15, according to the Globe. The Boston Symphony Orchestra, led by Andris Nelsons, was performing Mahler's Symphony No. 7 on Sept. 25 and 26, and the MFA was opening a retrospective of artist Suzanne Jackson on Sept. 26, the guide said. Lucy Raven's exhibition at the ICA Watershed was set to close Sept. 27.

stories.title: Man Set Off Explosive Device During Police Confrontation in Charlestown
stories.dek: Boston police said a man detonated a device worn around his neck early Monday near Mishawum and Main streets and was seriously injured before being taken into custody.
body: A man detonated an explosive device during a confrontation with Boston police officers in Charlestown early Monday and was seriously injured, according to police, as reported by Boston.com. He has been charged with possessing and discharging explosives, authorities said.

Police said officers were called to the area of Mishawum and Main streets at about 1 a.m. after the man reported that he did not feel safe there. Officers found him holding a device with wires running around his neck, and he told them it was explosive, according to a police incident report cited by Boston.com.

Members of the department's special operations team tried to disarm him using flash-bang devices and other less-lethal munitions, police said. According to the report, the man was struck several times but still set off the device, which exploded near his chest. Officers then took him into custody with the help of a K-9 unit.

The man was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital with serious injuries, according to Boston.com. Police said he told officers he did not intend to harm them. While he was being treated, he told officers there were more explosive materials in his vehicle, and the bomb unit searched the vehicle and towed it as evidence, police said.
Police did not release the man's name or age. The charges are allegations, and he is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

stories.title: Two Women Shot on Davidson Street in Hyde Park; One Critically Hurt
stories.dek: Boston police said two women were found with gunshot wounds early Saturday, one with life-threatening injuries, and no arrests had been made.
body: Two women were shot early Saturday on Davidson Street in Hyde Park, and one of them suffered life-threatening injuries, Boston police said, according to Boston.com.

Officers responded at about 1:10 a.m. to a report of a person shot at 114 Davidson St., police said. When they arrived, they found two women who had each been shot multiple times, according to the report.

Both women were taken to a local hospital, Boston.com reported. Police said one woman's injuries were considered life-threatening and the other's were not. Police did not release the names or ages of either woman.
Police did not describe the circumstances that led to the shooting, and the report did not include any information about a possible suspect or say whether the two women knew the person who fired.

As of Sunday night, no arrests had been made, police said. The investigation remains ongoing, and the department had not released any further information about what happened on Davidson Street, according to Boston.com.

stories.title: FBI Witnesses Detail Phone Evidence at Former Stoughton Officer's Trial
stories.dek: Federal investigators testified Friday about tens of thousands of messages and phone records in the trial of former Stoughton police detective Matthew Farwell.
body: Jurors in the federal trial of former Stoughton police detective Matthew Farwell heard testimony Friday from FBI investigators about messages, search records and phone activity recovered in the case, according to Boston.com's live coverage from the Moakley federal courthouse in Boston.

Farwell is charged with killing a witness or victim and with killing a child in utero. Prosecutors allege he killed a woman in early 2021 after learning she was pregnant with a child he believed was his, Boston.com reported. The woman was found dead in a Canton apartment. The defense contends she died by suicide. A state investigation initially reached that conclusion before a federal investigation led to Farwell's indictment, according to the report.

FBI digital forensic examiner Christopher Beckstrom testified that investigators recovered about 240,000 communications from the woman's devices, roughly 24,000 of them with Farwell, Boston.com reported. Under cross-examination, he agreed that she sent far more of those messages than Farwell did. He also described searches on a phone linked to Farwell and phone activity on the night of Feb. 1, 2021, the last day she was seen alive, according to the report.

Prosecutors say the woman had been an underage participant in a Stoughton police youth explorers program. Jurors heard messages that described sexual conduct when she was a minor, Boston.com reported. Kingston Police Chief Brian Holmes, a former Stoughton deputy chief, testified about an internal affairs investigation that found Farwell and other officers had engaged in inappropriate conduct with her.
FBI Special Agent Heidi Kelsch, who said the bureau interviewed about 130 people, was expected to continue testifying Monday. Farwell is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

stories.title: Friend and Stoughton Police Chief Testify at Farwell Federal Trial
stories.dek: A friend of the woman told jurors she urged Canton police to look at former detective Matthew Farwell after the death, the Boston Globe reported.
body: A close friend of the woman whose 2021 death is at the center of former Stoughton police detective Matthew Farwell's federal trial testified Thursday that she went to Canton police after the death and encouraged them to investigate Farwell, the Boston Globe reported.

Farwell, 40, is on trial in U.S. District Court in Boston before Chief Judge Denise J. Casper. Prosecutors allege he killed the 23-year-old woman, who was pregnant, in February 2021 to keep her from reporting crimes including an illegal sexual relationship that began when she was 15, according to the Globe. The defense argues she died by suicide. The state medical examiner first ruled the death a suicide and later changed the finding to undetermined, the newspaper reported.

The friend testified that the woman wanted to have Farwell's child and told her Farwell said the child was not his, according to the Globe. She said she spoke with the woman by phone days before her death and noticed nothing unusual.

Stoughton Police Chief Donna McNamara, who is on leave, testified that she did not know about a January 2021 call to the department concerning the woman until an FBI agent told her in 2024, the Globe reported. A digital forensic analyst testified about extracting data from the woman's devices, and the defense signaled it will argue that a manual review of her laptop altered data, according to the report. Kingston Police Chief Brian Holmes, a former Stoughton deputy chief, began testifying about the department's internal investigation.
Farwell has been held without bail since his August 2024 arrest and faces life in prison if convicted, the Globe reported. He is presumed innocent.

stories.title: Forensic Analyst and Police Officials Take the Stand in Farwell Trial
stories.dek: Thursday's testimony in the federal trial of former Stoughton detective Matthew Farwell covered device searches, a deleted station call recording and an internal investigation.
body: A state police digital forensics examiner, two current and former Stoughton police leaders, a Stoughton officer and a friend of the woman who died testified Thursday, the third day of testimony in the federal trial of former Stoughton police detective Matthew Farwell, Boston.com reported.

Farwell is charged with killing a witness or victim and killing a child in utero. The woman was found dead in her Canton apartment in February 2021. A state investigation first ruled the death a suicide, but an FBI investigation led to Farwell's indictment, according to the report. Farwell maintains she died by suicide after he ended their relationship, while prosecutors allege he killed her to keep her from speaking about the relationship and alleged misconduct.

Trooper Nicholas Guarino testified about accessing the woman's phone and laptop and said a search of Farwell's iPhone in February 2021 turned up nothing before it was returned, according to Boston.com. On cross-examination, he said some extraction data had been deleted as redundant and he could not find a report on a failed hard drive.

Former Stoughton Deputy Chief Brian Holmes, now Kingston's police chief, testified that a January 2021 call to the station from the woman's friend was recorded but later deleted automatically, the report said. Stoughton Chief Donna McNamara, on paid leave, reviewed attendance logs and the station call log. Prosecutors say Farwell grew worried after that call.

The friend testified that the woman seemed unhappy but not suicidal and that their last call was around 8:30 p.m. on Feb. 1, 2021, according to Boston.com. Holmes was scheduled to continue Friday. Farwell is presumed innocent.

stories.title: Former Healey Aide LaMar Cook Arrested on Federal SNAP Fraud Charges
stories.dek: Federal prosecutors allege the Springfield man, already facing a state drug trafficking case, collected food benefits after falsely reporting no income.
body: LaMar Cook, a former aide to Gov. Maura Healey who already faces state drug and gun trafficking charges, was arrested Wednesday on federal charges of SNAP fraud and wire fraud, the Boston Globe reported.

Prosecutors with the U.S. Attorney's Office in Massachusetts allege Cook, 46, of Springfield, received nearly $550 a month in federal food assistance after falsely claiming he had no income and less than $100 in the bank, according to the Globe. Prosecutors said his account held about $13,000 in January and more than $8,800 in April, and that he did not disclose that his fiancee, who lives with him, earned more than $80,000 from Springfield Public Schools.

Cook appeared before Judge Paul G. Levenson in federal court in Boston, where prosecutors asked that he be held for 10 days so Hampden County prosecutors could seek to revoke his bail in the state case, the Globe reported. The judge said he had to focus on the federal allegations and did not view them as a danger to the community, and Cook was released that afternoon. His public defender argued that Cook was not a flight risk.

Healey hired Cook in 2023 as deputy director of her Western Massachusetts office and fired him after his October 2025 arrest, according to the Globe. In that case, he has pleaded not guilty to charges stemming from the alleged seizure of about 17 pounds of cocaine that was to be delivered to the Springfield state building where he worked.
Healey said she was glad federal prosecutors were holding Cook accountable, the Globe reported. On social media, Cook said coverage had portrayed his finances unfairly. He is presumed innocent.

sources.title: LaMar Cook, former Healey aide facing drug trafficking case, arrested on federal SNAP fraud charges

stories.title: State Trooper Describes First Interview With Matthew Farwell at Trial
stories.dek: A state police investigator testified that the 2021 parking-lot interview with the former Stoughton detective was not recorded and that Farwell lied during it.
body: A Massachusetts State Police trooper testified Wednesday that investigators interviewed former Stoughton police detective Matthew Farwell in a school parking lot days after a woman's 2021 death and that Farwell lied during that conversation, Boston.com reported from Farwell's federal trial in Boston.

Farwell is charged with killing a witness or victim and killing a child in utero. The woman was found dead in her Canton apartment in February 2021, and a state investigation initially ruled the death a suicide before an FBI investigation led to his indictment, according to the report.

Trooper Matthew Dunne, assigned to the Norfolk County District Attorney's office, testified that investigators identified Farwell on surveillance footage on Feb. 6, 2021, and chose to interview him quickly and away from his home and workplace, Boston.com reported. The interview was not recorded and no notes were taken, which Dunne described as tactical decisions made by a supervisor. Dunne said Farwell told investigators he visited the woman on Feb. 1, 2021, to end their relationship, and that Farwell lied about when the relationship began and how often it was sexual.

Under cross-examination by defense attorney Kimberly Stevens, Dunne confirmed that DNA testing excluded Farwell as the father of the woman's unborn child, according to the report. The defense also pointed to the absence of signs of a struggle and to the woman's mental health history. Dunne acknowledged that some items at the scene were not collected and that neighbors were not interviewed.
A state toxicologist and Stoughton officer Robert Kuhn also testified, Boston.com reported. Testimony was set to resume Thursday. Farwell is presumed innocent.

stories.title: Second Defendant Pleads Guilty to Manslaughter in 2023 Mass and Cass Killing
stories.dek: A 41-year-old Boston woman was sentenced to six to eight years in prison for her role in the fatal stabbing of a 39-year-old woman on Topeka Street, prosecutors said.
body: A second defendant has pleaded guilty to manslaughter in the 2023 stabbing death of a 39-year-old woman near the area known as Mass and Cass, the Suffolk County District Attorney's Office said.

Crystal Morgan, 41, of Boston, pleaded guilty in Suffolk Superior Court and was sentenced by Judge Christopher Belezos to six to eight years in state prison, according to a release from the office. Her co-defendant, Michael Bellanti, 35, of Boston, pleaded guilty to manslaughter on Tuesday and was sentenced by Judge James Budreau to 10 to 15 years in state prison, prosecutors said.

According to prosecutors, an altercation involving the woman, Morgan and Bellanti began on the evening of Aug. 18, 2023, on Atkinson Street. Police broke up the dispute and separated the group, the release said.

Prosecutors said surveillance evidence showed Bellanti and Morgan later followed the woman onto Topeka Street, where Bellanti attacked her while Morgan held her. Both then left the area, according to the release. The woman died of her injuries on Aug. 27, 2023, prosecutors said.

District Attorney Kevin Hayden said the court received a statement from the woman's best friend describing her as a mother of three, a godmother and a close friend, according to the release. Hayden thanked the friend for helping the court see the woman's life beyond the circumstances of her death.

sources.title: Second person pleads guilty in 2023 stabbing of 39-year-old woman

stories.title: Elderly Couple Found Dead After Fire in Attleboro Home
stories.dek: Emergency responders conducting a wellness check found a married couple, 78 and 76, dead in an Andover Avenue house where a fire had burned, officials said.
body: A married couple in their 70s was found dead Wednesday inside their home on Andover Avenue in Attleboro after a fire, officials said, according to the Boston Globe.

Emergency responders went to the house just before 11:30 a.m. for a wellness check, the Globe reported. When they could not reach anyone inside, they forced their way into the home and found evidence of a significant fire, according to officials.

The fire was still smoldering on the first floor when responders entered, and crews had to put it out, the newspaper reported. The couple, a 78-year-old woman and a 76-year-old man, were found inside. Officials publicly identified them on Thursday.
Investigators determined that the fire was not suspicious, officials said, according to the Globe. The causes of the fire and of the couple's deaths remain under investigation, the report said.
The Globe's report did not say how long the fire may have burned before responders arrived or who requested the wellness check. Officials have not released any further information about the case.

stories.title: Police Seek Six People in South Station Tower Trespassing Case
stories.dek: Boston police said two groups entered the building at 680 Atlantic Avenue through an unlocked door in September and climbed a stairwell to the 52nd floor.
body: Boston police are asking the public to help identify six people they say trespassed at South Station Tower in September, according to a department community alert.

Investigators said the incident began at about 6:38 p.m. on Monday, Sept. 7, at the parking garage at 680 Atlantic Avenue, according to the alert. Police said four people entered through an unlocked service corridor door and took a stairwell up to the 52nd floor. Two more people followed a short time later, police said.

The first group stayed for about 45 minutes and the second for about 90 minutes, according to investigators. Police said the second group covered a security camera with a jacket before entering the floor. Both groups are believed to have left by a stairwell leading down toward the Amtrak terminal level, the alert said.
The department released two images in connection with the case. District A-1 detectives are reviewing the facts and circumstances, and no arrests were announced, according to police.

Anyone with information is asked to call District A-1 detectives at 617-343-4571. Tips, including photos and video, can be submitted anonymously by calling 1-800-494-TIPS, by texting the word TIP to 27463, or through the department's CrimeStoppers website, police said.

stories.title: Former School Colleague Testifies as Testimony Begins in Farwell Trial
stories.dek: A former assistant principal told jurors that reports the woman died by suicide did not fit the person she knew, the Boston Globe reported.
body: Testimony began Tuesday in the federal trial of former Stoughton police detective Matthew Farwell, with a former school administrator telling jurors that reports the woman at the center of the case had died by suicide did not make sense to her, the Boston Globe reported.

Prosecutors allege Farwell groomed the woman when she was a child in the Stoughton police Explorers program, began an illegal sexual relationship with her when she was 15 and he was 27, and killed her in 2021 to cover up those crimes, according to the Globe. The defense argues she was upset because Farwell was ending their relationship and that she died by suicide. Farwell has pleaded not guilty.

The former assistant principal at the Sharon elementary school where the woman worked as a teacher's aide testified that the woman was excited about her pregnancy, the Globe reported. She said she requested a wellness check when the woman missed work. On cross-examination, the defense questioned the woman's work record and the witness's membership in an online group seeking justice in the case.

Stoughton Det. Heather Cheever, who mentored the woman in the Explorers program, testified that the woman never expressed suicidal thoughts to her, according to the Globe. A property manager testified that she and a coworker reviewed security footage showing a masked, hooded figure later identified as Farwell, and a Canton officer described finding the woman during a well-being check.

Chief U.S. District Judge Denise J. Casper is presiding over the trial, which is expected to last about five weeks, the Globe reported. Farwell has been held without bail since his 2024 arrest and is presumed innocent.

sources.title: Sandra Birchmore's coworker testifies in Matthew Farwell trial that reports of her suicide 'didn't make sense.' Here's how the day unfolded.

stories.title: Man Accused of Grabbing Officer's Gun During South End Arrest
stories.dek: Boston police said a 34-year-old man wanted on two warrants fought officers and reached for a Taser and a firearm on Massachusetts Avenue on Sunday evening.
body: Boston police arrested a man Sunday evening in the South End who they say tried to take an officer's Taser and then grabbed an officer's firearm during a struggle on Massachusetts Avenue, according to a department release.

Officers from District D-4 responded at about 7:03 p.m. on Oct. 11 to a radio call reporting a group using drugs at the entrance of a private residence near 690 Massachusetts Avenue, police said. Officers recognized one man from a previous encounter, according to the release. Police said he gave a false name, and a records check showed he had two outstanding warrants.

When officers tried to arrest him, the man locked his hands together to avoid being handcuffed and fought with officers, police said. The struggle moved into the street amid heavy rain and traffic, according to the department. Police said he tried to take an officer's Taser and then grabbed an officer's gun, and officers pried his hand from the weapon before additional units helped take him into custody. The release did not mention any injuries.

Police identified the man as Felix Omar David Marrero, 34. He was expected to be arraigned in Roxbury District Court on charges including attempting to disarm a police officer, two counts of assault and battery on a police officer, resisting arrest and receiving stolen property, according to the release.
The outstanding warrants were issued by Suffolk Superior Court and Boston Municipal Court in drug distribution cases, police said. The charges are allegations, and he is presumed innocent.

sources.title: Violent Suspect Arrested for Attempting to Disarm Officers in Boston

stories.title: Criminal Investigation Underway After Fatal Crash on the Arborway
stories.dek: A 48-year-old SUV driver was killed Sunday when a sedan crossed the median on the Arborway in Jamaica Plain, according to reports.
body: The Suffolk County District Attorney's Office is conducting a criminal investigation into a crash on the Arborway in Jamaica Plain on Sunday that killed one driver and critically injured another, Boston.com reported, citing WHDH.

According to the reports, an 18-year-old driving a white sedan lost control, jumped the concrete median and collided with a red SUV traveling in the opposite direction. The SUV's driver, who was 48, was pronounced dead at the scene, Boston.com reported. Neither driver was named.

The 18-year-old was critically injured and taken to a local hospital, according to the report. Dash camera footage obtained by WHDH showed heavy damage to the driver's side of the SUV, Boston.com reported.

Sources told WHDH that the sedan was traveling at more than 50 mph on a stretch of road where the speed limit is 25 mph, according to Boston.com. The crash happened on a section of the parkway in Jamaica Plain, according to the report, which did not give a time.

The district attorney's office did not respond to a request for comment on Monday, Boston.com reported. A nearby resident told WHDH he was concerned that drivers treat the parkways like racetracks. No charges had been reported, and the investigation is ongoing.

sources.title: Criminal investigation reportedly underway after person killed in crash in Jamaica Plain

stories.title: Opening Statements Delivered in Federal Trial of Former Stoughton Detective
stories.dek: Prosecutors told jurors Matthew Farwell killed a woman to cover up years of abuse, while the defense said her 2021 death was a suicide, the Boston Globe reported.
body: The federal trial of former Stoughton police detective Matthew Farwell opened Friday with statements from prosecutors and defense attorneys at the Moakley U.S. Courthouse in Boston, the Boston Globe reported.

Farwell is charged with killing a woman to stop her from reporting federal crimes and with causing the death of her fetus, according to the Globe. He has pleaded not guilty and has been held without bail since his 2024 arrest. Chief U.S. District Judge Denise J. Casper is presiding, and a jury of 10 men and six women was seated for a trial expected to last about five weeks.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Torey B. Cummings told jurors that Farwell killed the woman in February 2021 at her Canton apartment and staged the scene to look like a suicide, the Globe reported. She argued that he had sexually abused the woman for years, beginning when she was a teenager, and that state police investigators had told the medical examiner the death was a suicide. DNA evidence has ruled out Farwell as the father of the baby, according to the report.

Defense attorney Kimberly C. Stevens acknowledged that Farwell made serious mistakes but said he did not kill the woman, according to the Globe. She argued that Farwell had ended the relationship and denied paternity, and that the woman, facing financial and emotional stress, took her own life. Stevens also challenged the forensic evidence.

Testimony was set to begin Tuesday, after the Monday holiday, with prosecutors planning to call six witnesses, including a Stoughton detective, a school administrator and officers who responded to the apartment, the Globe reported. Farwell is presumed innocent.

stories.title: Boston Man, 18, Charged With Murder in Hyde Park Avenue Shooting
stories.dek: Boston police arrested an 18-year-old Friday in the fatal shooting of a 20-year-old man at 1171 Hyde Park Avenue two days earlier.
body: Boston police on Friday arrested an 18-year-old Boston man and charged him with murder in a fatal shooting on Hyde Park Avenue earlier in the week, according to a department release.
Police identified the man as Christian Peebles, 18, of Boston. He was expected to be arraigned in West Roxbury District Court, the release said. Police did not describe how the arrest was made.

The shooting happened at about 5:09 p.m. on Wednesday, Oct. 7, at 1171 Hyde Park Avenue, according to police. Officers responding to a radio call for a person shot found a man with a gunshot wound, police said. He was taken to a local hospital, where he was pronounced dead. Police said the victim was 20.
The department's Homicide Unit continues to review the facts and circumstances of the case, according to the release. Police did not say what led to the shooting.

Anyone with information is asked to call the Homicide Unit at 617-343-4470, or to share tips anonymously by calling 1-800-494-TIPS or texting TIP to 27463, police said. stories.title: Brighton Man Arrested in Connection With Triple Stabbing
stories.dek: Boston police said a 24-year-old man stopped while carrying a machete on Western Avenue has been linked to the Oct. 4 stabbing of three men at Cambridge Street and Harvard Avenue.
body: Boston police have arrested a 24-year-old Brighton man and say they have linked him to a stabbing that injured three men in Brighton last weekend, according to a department release.

Officers and detectives from District D-14 responded at about 4:54 p.m. on Thursday, Oct. 8, to a radio call about a person swinging a large knife near Leo M. Birmingham Parkway and Waverly Street, police said. Officers stopped the man in front of 444 Western Avenue, and he dropped the knife when detectives ordered him to, according to the release. Police said they recovered a machete from the sidewalk and a folding knife from his pocket.

Police identified the man as Joshua Flores, 24, of Brighton. He was expected to be arraigned in Brighton District Court on charges of carrying a dangerous weapon and disturbing the peace, police said.

Detectives later developed probable cause linking Flores to a stabbing at about 1:30 a.m. on Sunday, Oct. 4, at Cambridge Street and Harvard Avenue, according to the release. Officers responding to that call found three adult men with stab wounds, and Boston EMS took them to local hospitals with injuries police described as not life-threatening.

In connection with that incident, Flores faces three counts of armed assault with intent to murder, three counts of assault and battery with a dangerous weapon causing serious bodily injury and two counts of mayhem, police said. The charges are allegations, and he is presumed innocent.

stories.title: Lawyers Recommend Excusing a Quarter of Jury Pool in Farwell Trial
stories.dek: Prosecutors and the defense jointly proposed dismissing 102 of 411 prospective jurors in the federal murder trial of former Stoughton detective Matthew Farwell, the Boston Globe reported.
body: Prosecutors and defense lawyers in the federal murder trial of former Stoughton police detective Matthew Farwell jointly recommended Wednesday that 102 of the 411 prospective jurors be excused, about a quarter of the initial pool, the Boston Globe reported.

Chief U.S. District Judge Denise J. Casper took the recommendation under advisement at a brief hearing, according to the Globe. Both sides were also reviewing questionnaires from 44 additional potential jurors. Jury selection began Tuesday, when prospective jurors filled out questionnaires that the court is keeping confidential, the newspaper reported.

Jurors who advance were due back Thursday for individual questioning, and Casper planned to seat 16 jurors, including four alternates, according to the Globe. Lawyers were told to be ready for opening statements Friday. Testimony is expected to last about five weeks, with more than 100 possible witnesses.

Farwell, 40, is charged in the death of a 23-year-old woman who was found in her Canton apartment on Feb. 4, 2021, and has pleaded not guilty, the Globe reported. Prosecutors allege he killed her to conceal years of crimes, including an illegal sexual relationship that began when she was 15. The defense says she died by suicide.

An initial investigation by Norfolk District Attorney Michael W. Morrissey's office concluded the death was a suicide, and the FBI arrested Farwell in 2024, according to the Globe. Farwell twice sought unsuccessfully to move the trial out of Massachusetts, arguing news coverage had affected the jury pool. He is presumed innocent.

stories.title: Cases Against Men Charged in Cambridge Brothel Ring End With Fees, Classes
stories.dek: More than 30 men accused of paying for sex through a ring based near Alewife had their charges dropped under standard agreements, but were publicly identified, the Boston Globe reported.
body: The last criminal cases against more than 30 men charged with paying for sex through a high-end brothel ring based near Alewife have concluded, with each man accepting a standard agreement that led to dismissal of the charges, the Boston Globe reported in a story published on Boston.com.

Under the agreements with Middlesex prosecutors, each man paid a $2,000 fee to advocacy groups, attended a program aimed at reducing demand for paid sex and agreed to stay away from sex workers, with the charges dropped after nine months, according to the Globe. The men did not admit wrongdoing and have no criminal records from the cases.

The ring operated out of luxury apartments in Cambridge and Watertown, and federal authorities described it as one of the most lucrative such networks on the East Coast, the Globe reported. Its three operators, Han Lee, James Lee and Junmyung Lee, who are not related, pleaded guilty to federal charges after arrests in November 2023, and Han Lee received the longest sentence, four years in prison.

Because buying sex is a state misdemeanor, the buyers were charged in state court through hearings that are usually closed, according to the report. A clerk magistrate opened them to the public, and the men lost a challenge at the Supreme Judicial Court. Authorities said they charged only men who had exchanged roughly 400 or more texts with the operators.

Unlike in earlier cases, the buyers were publicly identified, the Globe reported. Several lost their jobs, and a former Cambridge city councilor did not seek reelection. One advocate who works with women leaving the sex trade praised authorities' handling of the case, and legal observers called the outcome normal under state law.

body: Cambridge police responded Thursday morning to a report that a man had entered the women's locker room at the Planet Fitness in Porter Square and sexually assaulted people inside, Boston.com reported.

The report came in at about 9:10 a.m. on Oct. 1 at the gym at 1815 Massachusetts Ave., according to police. Officers located and apprehended a man police identified as Laquan Holland, Boston.com reported. The article did not list the charges he faces in connection with Thursday's incident.
Police did not say how many people were assaulted, according to the report. One person was taken to a hospital for evaluation.

Court records show Holland pleaded guilty in 2006 to two counts of child rape and one count of indecent assault and battery on a child under 14, Boston.com reported. He was taken into custody on Aug. 25, 2026, on a charge of failing to register as a sex offender, a charge that was later dismissed at the prosecution's request, according to the report.

Planet Fitness said it is committed to providing a safe environment for all members, that the franchise group canceled the man's membership and that it is cooperating with law enforcement, Boston.com reported. Cambridge police said the investigation is ongoing and had no further details as of Thursday evening. The new allegations have not been proven, and Holland is presumed innocent.

stories.title: Somerville Activates Displacement Fund After Teele Square Fire
stories.dek: A five-alarm fire at a three-story building on Broadway displaced 43 residents from 32 homes, and the city opened its emergency fund to help them, Boston.com reported.
body: Forty-three people were displaced by a five-alarm fire Wednesday in a three-story apartment building that spans 1137 to 1147 Broadway in Somerville's Teele Square, according to the Somerville Fire Department, as reported by Boston.com.

The fire began just before 5 p.m. on Sept. 30, the report said. Smoke first appeared on the third floor, and fire conditions were heavy above the ceiling, according to the fire department. Crews sent five aerial ladders to the roof and cut holes in it to release smoke. Firefighting operations were scaled back at about 10 p.m., Boston.com reported.

All occupants got out safely, and 32 homes were affected, according to the report. Several firefighters suffered minor injuries but were not taken to the hospital, the fire department said. The third floor and roof sustained fire, smoke and water damage, and the lower floors had extensive water damage. A laundromat, a smoke shop and a seafood restaurant on the ground floor were reported closed.

Departments from Arlington, Boston, Brookline, Belmont, Cambridge, Chelsea, Everett, Malden, Medford, Revere and Watertown assisted, while Stoneham covered Somerville's central fire station, according to Boston.com. Mayor Jake Wilson praised the responders and neighboring departments for preventing a worse outcome.
The city has activated its emergency displacement fund for affected residents, Boston.com reported. The cause of the fire has not been determined.

stories.title: Boston Police Cancel Public Appeal in Roxbury Stabbing Investigation

body: Boston police have canceled a community alert that asked the public to help identify a person in connection with a stabbing in Roxbury, saying detectives no longer need that assistance, according to an updated department release.

Officers from District B-2 responded at about 7:12 p.m. on Tuesday, Sept. 29, to a call for a person stabbed near 301 Warren Street, police said. Officers later found the victim in Kensington Park with a serious cut to the face, according to the release.

The victim was taken to a local hospital with injuries police described as not life-threatening, the release said. Officers searched the area for the person responsible but did not find anyone at the time, according to police.

The department had released three images of an individual it wanted to identify. The updated notice, marked as a cancellation, states that detectives are no longer seeking the public's help with the identification, though it does not say whether anyone has been identified or arrested.

District B-2 detectives are continuing to investigate, police said. Anyone with information can call detectives at 617-343-4275 or share tips anonymously by calling 1-800-494-TIPS, by texting the word TIP to 27463, or through the department's online CrimeStoppers page, according to the release.
